title: Ops Brief: Micro Playbook for Batch & Cache Configuration with Rollback Helpers
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Ship a compact, operation-focused micro-playbook panel in the Redwood Console adjacent to batch/cache config that helps operators safely apply recommended presets, preview expected cost/latency deltas, and perform fast rollback or canarying. The micro-playbook should be scannable (<=3 steps), include an explainable confidence indicator (why we recommended X), and provide one-click rollback and quick-links to rollback runbooks. This ticket drives the design spec, prototype, and usability testing for the panel.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with annotated components (panel header, recommendation card, delta preview, confidence strip, rollback button, canary toggle)
Interactive Figma prototype demonstrating: apply-recommendation flow, canary flow, rollback flow, and the in-panel explainers
Usability test completed with at least 6 platform engineers, documented issues and at least two iteration passes
Hand-off tokens: component CSS vars, copy snippets, and accessibility notes (contrast/keyboard flow)
Engineering tickets created for front-end, telemetry, and automation hooks
design_notes: Micro-playbook sits as a collapsible sidecar in Route > Model > Config (right rail) so operators can take action without full nav context switch
Primary CTA is 'Apply Recommendation' with secondary 'Preview Deltas' and tertiary 'Schedule Canary'
Recommendation card must surface three succinct rationales: workload pattern match, cost saving estimate, risk score (regression probability) with a link to the prompt test set used
Rollback flow offers immediate rollback (last-5-min snapshot) and a safe-rollback schedule (gradual revert over 10m) depending on current traffic
Confidence strip visualizes data sources: historical token distribution similarity, KV-cache hit prediction, and model quantization compatibility
Provide a compact changelog entry UI: brief auto-generated summary + free-text field for ops notes
Design for progressive disclosure: advanced knobs hidden behind 'Expert mode' to avoid operator overwhelm
Accessibility: ensure all control labels are explicit; slider semantics for canary percentage; color tokens not sole indicator of risk
tasks: Draft initial copy variations for recommendation rationales
Low-fidelity wireframes for three CTA variants
Run 6 moderated usability sessions with platform engineers
Incorporate feedback and produce final design tokens and component spec
Handoff to frontend with accessibility checklist and e2e scenario descriptions
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya T: Initial kickoff meeting notes: SREs want fast rollback, PM wants clear cost delta. Diego to wireframe three CTA patterns by 2026-03-06.

2026-03-05 - Diego A: Uploaded first wireframes. Two variants: inline preview vs modal preview. Leaning toward inline preview for context retention. Figured to include a small 'sanity-check' table comparing current vs proposed token-per-request median.

2026-03-07 - Priya N: Usability note from SRE review: Avoid burying rollback behind confirmation modals; prefer an immediate action with a soft 'Are you sure?' toast and the option to schedule rollback window.

2026-03-09 - Arjun P: Runtime constraint: can't compute exact KV-hit prediction in <200ms for long-tail keys; recommend we show probabilistic bucket (low/med/high) rather than precise percent to avoid misleading engineers.
2026-03-10 - Elena M: Research plan created. We'll run 6 sessions (3 junior engineers, 3 senior) and measure task completion, perceived trust, and time-to-decision.

2026-03-11 - Diego A: Prototype link shared in mockup_links. Added copy options for confidence language (e.g., 'recommended' vs 'suggested'). Need PM alignment on legal phrasing for 'guaranteed' terms.

2026-03-12 - Jared K: Please include telemetry events: recommendation_shown, preview_opened, apply_clicked, canary_started, rollback_initiated, rollback_confirmed. Also tag variations by model and route for later A/B analysis.
notes_for_engineering: Provide API hook: GET /recommendations?route_id={id}&workload_snapshot={ts} returns recommendation payload and risk score buckets
Telemetry contract: include scenario_id, recommendation_id, applied_by, canary_pct, rollback_reason (optional)
Front-end should be resilient to missing prediction fields: fallback to 'insufficient data' copy
Add feature flag to toggle micro-playbook for 10% of org for initial rollout
design_risks: Operators may over-rely on single-number estimates; mitigate with clear explainers and link to eval sets
Too many CTAs could cause hesitation — prioritize primary action and surface others in overflow
Real-time prediction latency might degrade UX if not cached; include optimistic UI with subsequent reconciliation
